title: Incidents and near-misses: primary evidence and publication revisions
ranking_basis: Revision integrity first, then complementary medical-device and deployment-inquiry evidence. This ranks research usefulness, not incident novelty or population risk.
interpretation_guards: Attribution is assertion-level: complainant, manufacturer, provider, regulator, respondent and court remedies are distinct.
Source family, collection, artifact, event, report, assertion and artifact revision are separate units.
Affected devices, requests, scans and administrative reports are not distinct injured people. Unknown harm and none reported are not established zero.
No unsupported near-miss count, fleet-wide rate, pooled incident total, clinical/legal advice or p(doom) conversion.
No personal names, VINs, contacts, locations, patient/personnel records, clinical particulars or narrative corpus.
Agency-authored portions do not relicense manufacturer submissions or third-party docket materials.

corrections.correction: Submitted six-new/two-enrichment labels were relative only to frozen 64 and are stale after item 13. NHTSA SGO and both correction claims already exist in ASI005; OpenAI sycophancy exists in ASI007.

NHTSA ODI is an additional investigation stream within an already cataloged NHTSA family. FDA, NZ OPC and NTSB are new named collection families; FTC enforcement is new within an already represented publisher.
No new incident follows from new source metadata. AIID4,619,665 are known index overlaps; exact AIM matches remain unverified.
NHTSA correction date differs from September 15 dictionary edition and October 8 retrieval. Missing before-text is unavailable.
FDA product contains AI; the cited recall does not isolate an AI-caused defect. Fifteen systems do not measure patient harm.
MAUDE supplement qualifies episode identification/date and mechanism; no complications reported is not independent zero harm or verified near miss.
openFDA device-event documentation has inconsistent 2009/1992 coverage statements. Successful API response retrieval was not established.
NZ inquiry edition May 2025 differs from June 4 publication; up to 13 failures is an estimate with 9 + 4 categories; 1735/1742 alerts remain conflicting; repeated scans are not people.
ODI 367 reviewed incidents includes 109 crashes; one injury and zero fatalities are case-scoped reported outcomes. Explicit duplicate SGO reports do not add events.
NTSB finding is multi-factor; June 2020 title-only reissue does not change causality.
FTC allegations remain allegations despite a stipulated remedy; Everalbum deletion compliance is respondent-reported, not an independent audit.
Anthropic affected-request fractions retain provider attribution and time-window/population; status API 50 limit is not historical completeness.
OpenAI two 2025 artifacts describe one preexisting episode. March 2023 1.2% is conditional potential exposure, not all users or verified harm.
Agency hosting, public availability and consumer terms do not provide a blanket right to republish third-party narratives or postmortem bodies.

Separate allegations, neither-admit-nor-deny terms, remedy, case status and respondent-reported compliance. Starting URLs: https://www.ftc.gov/system/files/ftc_gov/pdf/DE019-StipulatedOrderforPermanentInjunctionandOtherRelief.pdf ; https://www.ftc.gov/system/files/ftc_gov/pdf/paravision_compliance_report_redacted.pdf. Return verified URLs and page/section locators, exact attribution and units, dates, artifact-specific rights, duplicate links, corrections and unresolved holds; report negative or inaccessible results honestly. Stop after this bounded question is answered or access is unavailable. No login, outreach, bypass, bulk download, sensitive patient/personnel records, names, VINs, locations, clinical particulars, manufacturer narrative corpus, source code/model/target execution, repository edits, live collection, canonical import, deployment, legal/medical advice or p(doom) conversion.
